research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing at 2 FR 1191 (Federal Register of June 11, 1937, govinfo file FR-1937-06-11, PDF page 1; text layer, recorded as acceptable as original). The page carries two orders: Executive Order 7627 (revocation of Executive Order No. 6120, California, signed June 8, 1937) and Executive Order 7628. Executive Order 7628 is headed "WITHDRAWAL OF PUBLIC LAND", Arkansas, is signed at The White House June 8, 1937, and is followed by the filing line F. R. Doc. 37-1714, Filed June 9, 1937; the bracketed number is garbled by OCR ([No. 76281) and the American Presidency Project text (node 368980) agrees with the heading, date and body. Inventory correction: the registered clause extent (characters 764-1178 of the original file) is the text of Executive Order 7627, not 7628. The real order is characters 1372-2273: the enacting words, section 1, section 2 and section 3. It is treated as one clause because it commands one thing on one tract: section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935 as to a single tract (T. 4 S., R. 28 W., Fifth Principal Meridian, sec. 31, lots 1 and 5 of NW1/4, 79.50 acres) and was self-executing on signing, and sections 2 and 3 temporarily withdrew that tract from settlement, location, sale or entry for classification until revoked by the President or by act of Congress. The withdrawal is the only continuing command. Ending: Executive Order 7719, signed October 8, 1937 (printed at 2 FR 2465, Federal Register of October 12, 1937), includes the same tract (T. 4 S., R. 28 W., sec. 31, lots 1 and 5 of NW1/4, 79.50 acres) in the Ouachita National Forest and states "The reservation made by this order supersedes the tem" [soft hyphen and line break] "withdrawal of the above-described land made by" "Executive Order No. 7628 of June 8, 1937." The text layer interleaves neighbouring columns (the Camas refuge sentence of another order sits next to this sentence); the American Presidency Project text of Executive Order 7719 reads it in one piece, and the tract description matches. Executive Order 7719 has no effective-date wording, so the end is dated on signing, 1937-10-08 (a reading, disclosed). Status proposal (NO, rationale in the separate status decision): the withdrawal ended on that date and nothing in the held sources revives it. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches. The U.S. Code search (release point current through 2026-10-09, with later laws through 2026-10-14 not reflected) and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) both complete with no hit for this number; they serve to show no current provision gives the withdrawal continuing force. The OFR catalog search records the supersession by Executive Order 7719 and the note that this order amends Executive Order 6964. The held-text number search found this number in the texts of Executive Orders 7719, 7720 and 7721, all on the same Federal Register page; only 7719 concerns this tract. The 1989 printed codification lists this order under public lands as excluded, not ended, which is not evidence of continuing effect. The listed gap 'target provision not located: EO:7721' concerns the neighbouring order 7721 on that page, which has no sentence about this tract.
savings_reason: Executive Order 7719 includes the same 79.50-acre tract in the Ouachita National Forest, a separate reservation made under the Act of March 3, 1891 and the Act of June 4, 1897. The land therefore remains reserved under that independent order after the temporary withdrawal ended; nothing in Executive Order 7719 preserves Executive Order 7628 itself or its section 3 duration clause.
earlier_end_check: Candidate earlier ends examined. Section 3 says the withdrawal "shall continue in force until revoked by the President or by" act of Congress, so there is no fixed term or sunset. No instrument between June 8 and October 8, 1937 revokes or supersedes the order: the OFR disposition notes name only the supersession by Executive Order 7719, and the held-text search finds no other order naming this number. Section 1's revocation of Executive Order No. 6964 as to the tract was performed on signing and is not a cessation of the withdrawal in section 2.
scope_check: One clause. Executive Order 7719 supersedes the withdrawal of "the above-described land", which is the whole tract withdrawn by section 2 (the same 79.50 acres), so it is a supersession of the entire continuing command and not of a part. Executive Order 7719 adds other lands to the forest, which do not concern this order.
independent_command_check: The order has one continuing command, the temporary withdrawal in sections 2 and 3. Section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 6964 as to the tract and was exhausted on signing; the revocation of the earlier order's effect on this tract is a surviving consequence, not a continuing command of this order.
savings_check: Executive Order 7719 contains no wording preserving Executive Order 7628. The land stays reserved under Executive Order 7719 (state continuing_independent); rights acquired under the withdrawal were limited by its own words 'Subject to all valid existing rights'.
